title: Path Sum III
spaceBreakdown:
- unordered_map<long long,int> seen: up to n entries (one per node on the current root-to-leaf path, plus the seed) → O(n)
- recursion call-stack depth: worst case O(n) for a skewed tree, O(log n) for balanced
- not counted: input tree, returned int
approach: Use a prefix-sum hash map during a single DFS. Maintain the running sum from the root to the current node; for each node, the number of valid paths ending there equals how many ancestor prefix sums equal `runningSum - targetSum`. Store prefix-sum frequencies in a hash map, increment on entry, and decrement on exit (backtrack) so that sibling subtrees don't contaminate each other. Running sums can reach 1000 × 10^9 = 10^12, so use `long long`.
hints: If you knew the sum from the root down to every node, what arithmetic relationship between two of those sums would identify a downward path whose sum equals targetSum? A path must travel from an ancestor to a descendant.

Use a prefix-sum frequency map during DFS. At the node with value 5 under root 10 (running sum 15) with targetSum 8, look up 15 − 8 = 7 in the map; each prior prefix sum of 7 marks one valid path ending here.

```
dfs(node, runningSum):
    if node is null: return
    runningSum += node.val
    count += map[runningSum - targetSum]
    map[runningSum] += 1
    dfs(node.left, runningSum)
    dfs(node.right, runningSum)
    map[runningSum] -= 1
```

**Empty tree** - root is null
`Input: root = [], targetSum = 0` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: accessing node->val before the null check → undefined behavior / crash

**Single-node hit** - the only node equals targetSum
`Input: root = [8], targetSum = 8` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: not seeding the map with {0:1} → returns 0 (no prefix sum 0 to match the root-to-itself path)

**All zeros** - every downward subpath sums to 0
`Input: root = [0,0,0], targetSum = 0` → `Expected: 5`
⚠️ Bug: skipping the `map[runningSum] -= 1` backtrack step → returns 6 (left-child prefix sums leak into the right-child subtree)

**Negatives with duplicate prefix sums** - the same prefix sum recurs at different depths
`Input: root = [1,-1,1,-1], targetSum = 0` → `Expected: 4`
⚠️ Bug: using a set instead of a map (counting each prefix sum once) → returns 3 (misses the second occurrence of prefix sum 0)

followUps.q: What if the tree has up to 10^5 nodes instead of 1000?
followUps.a: The same prefix-sum hash map DFS runs in O(n) time and O(n) space, so it scales directly. No algorithmic change is needed; just ensure `long long` for running sums since 10^5 × 10^9 = 10^14.

followUps.q: What if you must return every valid path (the node lists), not just the count?
followUps.a: Same DFS, but when `map[runningSum - targetSum] > 0`, record the path segment from each matching ancestor to the current node. In the worst case (all zeros, targetSum 0) there are O(n^2) paths, so time and output space become O(n^2).

followUps.q: What if the path can travel in any direction (up or down) as long as it is simple?
followUps.a: Downward-only prefix sums no longer suffice. Use centroid decomposition: for each centroid, count paths passing through it using a prefix-sum map, then recurse into subtrees. This gives O(n log n) time and O(n) space.
